name: Blister steel by cementation

name: Ophthalmoscope

name: Secure mercury supply
note: Almaden is an imperial monopoly, so this is a political node before it is a technical one. name: Drawn tube production
note: Anneal a tube, coat with soap as lubricant, draw it through a die on a water-powered wire draw to reduce diameter and thicken walls uniformly. Much slower than rolling but gives excellent surface finish and precise dimensions. The soaped tube must be perfectly round or it jams in the die.

name: Pneumatic rock drill
note: A small piston driven by compressed air strikes a hardened bit repeatedly against rock, advancing into the hole while the operator rotates it slightly between blows. name: Trip hammer and water-driven forge hammer
note: A cam on a water wheel shaft lifts a heavy hammer, then the cam releases it and gravity and the impact do the forging work. Much faster than hand hammering and the work is uniform. The key is that the head must be hard iron or the repeated impact will deform it; case-hardening is necessary to survive. Rome has this; it is the foundation of heavy forge work.

name: Nitric acid
note: Saltpetre plus oil of vitriol, distilled. Unlocks aqua regia, silver nitrate (hence photography and silvered mirrors), etching, nitrates and, if you choose it, high explosives. The brown fumes will kill anyone who breathes them and the damage is delayed by hours.

name: Seismograph (earthquake measurement)
note: Heavy mass damped by springs or pendulum. Frame sits on ground. Relative motion drives pen against rotating drum. Natural period of 10-20 seconds maximizes sensitivity to distant earthquakes.

name: Calotype negative-positive
note: The negative is the invention. Paper negative allows unlimited prints from one exposure. Cheaper than daguerreotype.

name: Newspaper institution
note: Daily publication breaks state monopoly on information. Political instrument. Cheap accurate copying enables rapid idea spread.

name: Wet collodion plate
note: Glass plate coated with collodion. Exposed wet. Huge leap in sensitivity and speed. Must develop within minutes.

name: High voltage transmission
note: Power loss in a wire is proportional to I squared; raising voltage and lowering current for the same power reduces losses dramatically. Remote hydro becomes economic only with high voltage. Requires transformers, insulators, and careful design.

name: Substation and distribution
note: Receives high-voltage transmission lines, steps them down via transformers to local distribution voltage, distributes to neighborhoods and industries. A hub between generation and use; switching and protection equipment required.
